Bug_Title: FE: Doomed test for equality to NaN (FE_TEST_IF_EQUAL_TO_NOT_A_NUMBER)
Bug_Details:
This code checks to see if a floating point value is equal to the special
Not A Number value (e.g., if (x == Double.NaN)). However,
because of the special semantics of NaN, no value
is equal to Nan, including NaN. Thus,
x == Double.NaN always evaluates to false.

To check to see if a value contained in x
is the special Not A Number value, use
Double.isNaN(x) (or Float.isNaN(x) if
x is floating point precision).
 if (x == Double.NaN) NaN Nan NaN x == Double.NaN x Double.isNaN(x) Float.isNaN(x) x
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where it checks if a floating point value is equal to the special Not A Number value (NaN). However, because of the special semantics of NaN, no value is equal to NaN, including NaN. Therefore, x == Double.NaN always evaluates to false.
Trigger_Explanation: The method showBug from the NaNChecker class is called with Double.NaN as a parameter. This triggers the bug because the method checks if the input value is equal to Double.NaN, which is not possible as per the Java specification for the Not a Number value.
